issues.description: The problem statement and tests expect a function named simulate_msd_one_round(n_shots: int, p: float) but the template defines a function named simulate_one_round(...) (and raises an error message referring to simulate_msd_one_round). This name/signature mismatch is structural: code that imports or tests simulate_msd_one_round will fail or be confusing because the template uses a different function name.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template function simulate_one_round to simulate_msd_one_round so its name matches the problem specification and tests, or add a thin wrapper simulate_msd_one_round that calls simulate_one_round. Ensure the parameter order and names match the specification: (n_shots: int, p: float) -> tuple[float, float].

issues.description: The one-round simulation function is referred to as simulate_msd_one_round in the problem statement and used by plot_msd, but the template implementation provides a function named simulate_one_round. The solution implements simulate_msd_one_round. This name mismatch between the template and the problem/solution will confuse students and break references (e.g., plot_msd) that expect simulate_msd_one_round.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template function simulate_one_round to simulate_msd_one_round (and update any internal references) so the template matches the problem statement and the solution. Ensure plot_msd and any callers use the same name.
